m=await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='task-ad530a4b separator-adjacent anomaly marking: demonstrated rules, test unresolved',content='''Continual ARC task-ad530a4b. Demos show a full separator line in color 2 and a uniform field/background. A small anomaly/object is associated with an output full line of color 8 parallel to the separator. Demonstrations: (1) 30x29, separator vertical at c12, 6-rectangle at c13-14 rows7-23, output leaves object unchanged and adds full-height 8 at c15. (2) 17x19, vertical sep c14, irregular 5 object c6-11 rows6-16; output object translated right +2 to c8-13 (adjacent to separator) and adds 8 stripe at c7. (3) 6x29 horizontal separator row5, single 6 at (r3,c13); output 8 full row3 and 6 at row4. (4) 18x11 horizontal sep row15; 9 cells at row13; output row13 becomes full 8 and anomaly moves to row14. (5) vertical sep c23, 7 object c15-22 already adjacent; output adds full-height 8 at c14, object unchanged. (6) horizontal sep row5, 3 segment at row2; output changes original anomaly row2 back to background, places 3 segment at row4 adjacent to separator, and full 8 stripe row3. Likely general idea: move anomaly toward separator to contact it, and draw an 8 stripe marking an intermediate/adjacent original position; if already touching, draw stripe just outside object on far side. However test with 7 irregular silhouette at rows9-17, cols1-4, vertical separator c13 remained unsolved despite 8 submissions. Tried stripes at c0, c5, c2, c8, c4 and combinations with moving motif (incl translating +8), all reported wrong. Do not reuse these guesses blindly; request demos and derive exact mapping / distinguish object anomaly from full-color shape. Preserve exact dimensions and separator. Highly useful: stripe location/translation varies in demos, so rule may depend on object shape or distance and simple 'move to divider plus adjacent stripe' was not sufficient for the test.''',global_=True)
m
